newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - Oct 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - Oct 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- FAYEDS TAKE 80 MILLION STG FROM HARRODS

According to Harrod's annual report, the Fayed brothers have taken more than 80 million stg out of the luxury department store. Mohamed Al-Fayed and his brother Ali paid a 40 million stg dividend into their Alfayed Investment and Trust Private Limited Partnership in Bermuda from Harrods Holdings and the company repaid a 40.9 million stg subordinated loan from the brothers and replaced it with bank debt.
-- UNITED PLANS 480 MILLION STG OFFER FOR BLENHEIM

United News and Media is considering a 480 million stg bid for Blenheim Exhibitions in an effort to prevent the Dutch publisher VNU from raising its stake in the company to 24.9 per cent. Observers expect United's chief executive Lord Hollick to press ahead with trying to gain the business. VNU has reserved its position on what it will do if a rival bid emerges.
-- SAUDI CLOSE TO LONRHO'S PRINCESS

Saudi billionaire Prince Al-Waleed is poised to clinch his position as favourite bidder for Lonrho's Princess hotel chain. Chief executive of the multi-national mining-to-property conglomerate, Dieter Bock, is expected to grant the prince exclusive negotiating rights lasting up to three months to buy the chain for 350 million stg.
-- HEPWORTH TO SELL REFRACTORIES ARM

The building materials company chaired by Professor Roland Smith, Hepworth, is to put its refractories division on the market. The company hopes to complete the sale before the end of the year. Merchant bank Schroders have prepared a memorandum of sale. Interested parties could include Radex-Heraklith, Global Industrial Technology, Lafarge and CinVen.
-- CRUCIBLE CLEARS DECKS FOR MAJOR PURCHASE

The engineering group Morgan Crucible is planning to float a portfolio of its smaller engineering businesses as a move to clear the decks to look for a major acquisition. The group has appointed Panmure Gordon as broker for a float, which should value the new business at 50 million stg.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- BILLIONAIRE BRANSON TO BID FOR FOUR RAIL FRANCHISES

Virgin, owned by Richard Branson, is to attempt to turn his group into one of Britain's top railway owners by biding for four rail franchises. Within three years the group will bid for the Cross Country franchise and the West Anglia Great Northern franchise. It is also prepared to bid for the West Coast Main Line and Thameslink.
-- SMITH TAKES THE HOT SEAT AT MORGAN

The head of development capital at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Robert Smith, is to take over at Morgan Asset Management following the resignation of four top executives in the wake of the Peter Young affair. Many expected DMG to go outside the group for a high-profile name from the fund-management industry, or have a German imposed on it from Deutsche Bank's Frankfurt headquarters.
-- BA -AMERICAN LINK POISED FOR LANG APPROVAL

British Airways is expected to win approval from the UK government for its alliance with American Airlines, which will open the way to the creation of the world's foremost airline group. Airline and Whitehall insiders expect Ian Lang, board of trade president, to give the go ahead for the deal. BA will have to surrender a number of take-off and landing slots at Heathrow to reduce its share of the transatlantic market.
-- ROVER WANTS TO SHAKE-UP TO SAFEGUARD 5,000 JOBS

Carmaker Rover is to ask its unions to agree to a flexibility programme to secure 5,000 jobs that will otherwise be threatened by the planned overhaul of its Longbridge plant in Birmingham. Rover's new chief executive Walter Hasselkus and his management team want to maintain job levels by transferring workers from Longbridge to the Land Rover factory at Solihull, where output is rising.
-- STRONG GROWTH PUSHES POUND TOWARDS DM2.50

According to a survey by the British Chambers of Commerce, the manufacturing industry has experienced a leap in new orders from the home market. It shows that industry is beginning to grow strongly on the back of rising domestic demand. The news is set to buoy the pound, which has risen to its highest level for two years, helped by Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's speech at the Conservative Party conference.
THE OBSERVER
-- EUROTUNNEL RESCUE UNDER THREAT

French shareholders are threatening to ruin Eurotunnel's rescue plan and force the Channel operator into bankruptcy. According to a powerful private shareholders' group, the French are outraged by financial reconstructuring, which could lead to the banks owning 75 per cent of Eurotunnel. Adacte, the Paris- based action group, is trying to rally French investors to vote against the rescue package.
-- EMPLOYERS RELYING ON TEMPORARY STAFF TO FILL VACANCIES

According to the latest index from Reed Personnel Services, employers demand for temporary staff is increasing faster than for permanent staff. One of Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's wise men, Professor Patrick Minford, expressed concern that the move to temporary staff is hindering the recovery. Executive chairman of Reed, Alec Reed, said the figures show the extent of the structural change that is taking place in the labour market.
-- WICKES CHIEFS TO CONSIDER BONUS REFUND

Former chairman of DIY retailer Wickes, Henry Sweetbaum, and his two former executive colleagues, Trefor Llewellyn and Michael Corner, are considering repaying some of their profit-related bonuses as the responsibility for the group's 50 million stg overstatement of profits. Performance bonuses were not deserved because the group's earnings were overstated for at least four years.
-- SPENDING PAVES WAY FOR TAX CUT

According to Whitehall insiders, revised Government borrowing forecasts will allow Chancellor Kenneth Clarke to take one pense stg off the basic tax rate in the Budget. Officials are encouraged by the rising tax receipts following the pick up in consumer spending and believe Clarke will be able to reduce taxes while presenting his measures as fiscally responsible.
-- NEW FIGHT FOR LLOYDS CHEMIST

The Office of Fair Trading is set to accept bids for Lloyds Chemist by Unichem and Gehe now they have decided to sell wholesale depots. The Monopolies and Mergers Commission insisted that Unichem sell six wholesaling depots and Gehe seven. Renewal of the bids comes despite last week's announcement by Lloyds that pre-tax profits fell by 8.6 million stg. -- BMC +44 71 377 1742
